goal: Hook: pull classroom toys from a bag one at a time and describe one aloud; pose "What is it, and what do we use it for?"; set up knee-to-knee partners, step 1 (sit facing, say one thing).
note: Toys and objects are the classroom's, never from home. Knee-to-knee partners is taught over days 1 to 3 and kept all year. ELA lean ek-discussion: ELA grade K unit 1 teaches discussion rules alongside from its day 1.

goal: Knee-to-knee steps 2 and 3: listen to the partner, then say back one thing they said, on "This is a ___" with a classroom object in hand.
note: Teacher models the say-back with the class puppet first. ELA lean ek-describe-aloud is ELA grade K unit 2 (later): the teacher models describing aloud with the object in hand.

goal: Knee-to-knee rounds with center objects: say what it is, the partner says it back; three rounds, partners swap.
Hear one page of the ELA toy book again and point to the picture of its topic; name the word "topic" as what the whole page is about.
note: Host: ELA grade K unit 1, Toys and play (days 1 to 34); ek-main-topic alongside. The page is reread, not taught as a reading lesson; reading stays in ELA.

goal: Meet the text map: with the teacher, draw the toy page's topic in the middle box and two facts beside it, and say them.
note: Model: text map, K to 1 stage, introduced (topic as a picture with two facts beside it).

goal: Take apart one sentence from the toy page with "It has ___" and rebuild it from word cards; its job is to tell a fact about the topic.
note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day. ELA lean ek-sentences is ELA grade K unit 2 (later): this unit teaches its own pattern orally and on the page, with no lesson on capitals or end marks. Replay tool for "It has ___" optional (paper path: the teacher reads it).

goal: Say "It has ___" about five classroom objects with picture word cards; partners build the sentence from the cards and say it back.
Add "It can ___" for what a toy does, and sort the class's sentences into a part ("It has") or an action ("It can").
Describe a classroom object to a partner with what it is, its color and what we use it for ("We use it to ___"), using color and size words.
note: Home language: name the object in the home language first; the teacher names cognates (color and color).

goal: Color and size word work: sort picture cards by color and by big or small, then say one sentence about a card.
Find-it game: describe a classroom object on the table so a partner can find it and point to it (the audience can see the object).
note: Change of audience, part 1: a partner who can see the object.

goal: Give one direction and follow one direction back ("Put it on the shelf", "Put it next to the box") with the classroom object.
Knee-to-knee rounds: describe a center object, give one direction, and the partner follows it.
Say the topic and two facts aloud from the text map for three classroom objects, with the frames each entry point keeps.
Mid-unit assessment: each child describes a new classroom object to the teacher (what it is, two facts, what we use it for) while partners play the find-it game.
note: About a minute a child for 30 children over the period; anyone not heard is heard in the first ten minutes of the next day. Response time: the first ten minutes of the next day, in groups from the sheet. Look-fors per entry point.

goal: After ten minutes of regrouping from the mid-unit sheet, build an all-about page with the teacher: the topic drawn, two facts drawn and labeled.
note: The model page Curio Class writes for the unit; teacher thinks aloud while drawing.

goal: Labels: what a label does (names a part), and label the model page's parts with the teacher.
Match label cards to the parts of pictured toys and say each label in an "It has ___" sentence.
Hear a second toy page from the ELA book; with a partner, find its topic and two facts on a text map and tell them back.
Draw and label an own all-about page on a classroom toy, with the frame each entry point keeps.
note: First application day. Candidate kept (California 1.26, all four domains in the unit): listening (days 4 and 19), speaking (every day), the shared reading (days 4 and 19), drawing and labeling (today); 0 days added. Withdrawal: entry points 5 and 6 work without the sentence frame from the next day.

goal: Describe the same object to a partner who cannot see it (it is hidden in a bag), then say what you added because they could not see it.
note: Change of audience, part 2, and noticing what changed (bar item 10).

goal: Build sentences from shuffled cards ("This is / it is / it has / it can / we use it to") and say them to a partner.
Talk about language: say what "It has" does (it tells a fact) and check own sentences against the unit goal with thumbs and the teacher's picture checklist.
note: Bar item 12 (oral self-check this unit; the self-check page starts in unit 2, as its candidate cell sets).

goal: Make alone: draw and label a second all-about page about a different classroom object, then tell it to a partner.
note: Withdrawal: last framed day for entry points 3 and 4 (frames off for the end-of-unit telling and drawing or writing task); entry points 1 and 2 keep the picture word bank and lose the cloze frame from the end-of-unit assessment.

goal: Describe a toy and say its topic and two facts with the picture word bank only.
note: Oral rehearsal of the unit forms with the picture word bank only; no new form.

goal: Partner share: tell your page to a partner, who says back one fact; add or fix one label.
Find-it rounds with hidden objects: describe, the partner guesses, then swap.

End-of-unit assessment: hear a new page about a classroom object and point to its topic and its facts; draw and label a page about a new object; the teacher hears the first half of the talk tasks (tell the teacher about a new object).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 1 of 2 (about 30 minutes): the heard part and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the teacher hears about 15 talk tasks, about a minute each, while the others work. Look-fors per entry point on the paper sheet, "seen" or "not yet"; each item asks about each part of each code listed. The new page is Curio Class's own, invented for practice. Candidate kept (PRIME Match.LE): the heard page carries one interpretive item, point to the topic, inside today; 0 days added.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the second half of the talk tasks (tell the teacher about a new object: what it is, two facts, what we use it for).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 2 of 2: the other 15 talk tasks; students not being heard finish and check their page against the self-check. Each student is heard once.

goal: Respond: regroup from the sheet and reteach the "not yet" forms ("It has", "It can", labels) on the toys; groups rehearse the describing turn.
note: Respond day for the end-of-unit assessment: at most four groups from the sheet's "not yet" cells, by form and by entry point; the others rehearse in pairs from the frame.

goal: Hook: drawn pictures of the class's morning walk; pose "What happened first, next and at the end?" and tell the walk with the teacher in two pictured steps.
note: The class event is one the whole class saw, so no one needs home details; the teacher may take their own photos.

goal: Tell a class event in two steps with "Today we ___. Then we ___." and say back one thing the partner did.
note: ELA lean ek-describe-aloud: ELA grade K unit 2 (days 35 to 76) runs alongside from school day 35.

goal: Knee-to-knee: tell the morning walk in two pictured steps, and the partner says back one thing they did.
Hear ELA unit 1's story of two friends sharing a toy again and name its character and what happens first and at the end.
note: Bridge (frame "If later"): ELA reads its weather stories from ELA day 49, so days 31 to 48 use class events and this already-heard toy story.

goal: Meet the story map (three pictures in a row: first, next, at the end) and fill it with the teacher from the toy story.
note: Model: story map, K to 1 stage, introduced.

goal: Name a story's stages openly: a start, a middle and an end, moved on by time words (first, next, at the end).
note: Candidate kept (PRIME Depth.KLU, the stages of a story named openly): today, 0 days added.

goal: Retell the toy story in three parts from the story map with picture cards, partners taking turns.
Take apart a story sentence with the past tense (went, saw, ran, said) and rebuild it; its job is to tell what already happened.
note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day.

goal: Past tense rounds: say what the class did yesterday with went, saw and ran picture cards.
Learn what "and then" joins (two things that happened, in order) and put it into the two-step telling.
Tell a second class event (the class visitor) in two steps with "and then"; the partner says back one thing.
Tell the class event to a partner who was there.
note: Change of audience, part 1.

goal: Tell the same event to a visitor who was not there (another adult or the class puppet), then say what you added for them.
note: Change of audience, part 2, and noticing what changed.

goal: Feeling words: happy and sad, and find on the story map how the friends felt at the start and at the end ("At the end she was happy").
note: Entry points 5 and 6 add a "because" to the feeling line.

goal: Sort feeling and time word cards and act out happy and sad with a sentence for each.
Mid-unit assessment: each child tells the teacher a new class event in two pictured steps while partners retell the toy story.
note: About a minute a child; anyone not heard goes first next day. Response time: the first ten minutes of the next day, in groups from the sheet.

goal: After ten minutes of regrouping from the mid-unit sheet, retell the toy story in three parts on a story map with a partner, adding a feeling word.
Retell rehearsal with three picture cards and the frames each entry point keeps.
Hear the ELA weather story again and take apart its opening: who the character is and where the story starts.
note: ELA grade K unit 2 reads its weather stories from ELA day 49 (school day 49); the weather story is taken apart from today.

goal: Take apart the weather story's ending and the time words that move it on.
Retell the weather story in three parts on a story map with a partner.
Build a short shared story with a character with the teacher: what happens first, next and at the end, on a story map.
note: Own-story prompt (APPROACH "Sensitive ground"): a home or family prompt is one of several; an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed; a story may be told first in the home language.

goal: Build "First ___. Next ___. At the end ___." sentences from cards about the shared story and say them.
Plan an own short story with a character on a story map with a partner: talk first, then draw the three parts.
note: First application day. Own-story prompt (APPROACH "Sensitive ground"): a home or family prompt is one of several; an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed; a story may be told first in the home language. Withdrawal: entry points 5 and 6 work without the sentence frame from the next day.

goal: Tell your story to a partner from your story map and add a time word to each picture.
Talk about language on the first self-check page: what "and then" does, then check own telling against the page.
note: Self-check page (kept by the student): name the form and its job in own words, then judge own language against the unit goal. Candidate kept (bar item 12, the self-check page's first use): today, 0 days added.

goal: Make alone: tell and draw an own story with a character in three parts, labeled with time words.
note: Own-story prompt (APPROACH "Sensitive ground"): a home or family prompt is one of several; an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed; a story may be told first in the home language. Withdrawal: last framed day for entry points 3 and 4 (frames off for the end-of-unit telling and drawing or writing task); entry points 1 and 2 keep the picture word bank and lose the cloze frame from the end-of-unit assessment.

goal: Retell a story with the picture word bank only, partners taking turns.
note: Oral rehearsal of the unit forms with the picture word bank only; no new form.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: hear a new short weather story and order three pictures; tell and draw an own story; the teacher hears the first half of the retells.
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 1 of 2 (about 30 minutes): the heard part and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the teacher hears about 15 talk tasks, about a minute each, while the others work. Look-fors per entry point on the paper sheet, "seen" or "not yet"; each item asks about each part of each code listed. The new weather story is Curio Class's own, invented for practice. Own-story prompt (APPROACH "Sensitive ground"): a home or family prompt is one of several; an invented character or a chosen place is always allowed; a story may be told first in the home language.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the second half of the retells (retell the new story to the teacher in three parts).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 2 of 2: the other 15 talk tasks; students not being heard finish and check their page against the self-check. Each student is heard once.

goal: Respond: reteach past tense, "and then" and the time words in groups from the sheet; groups rehearse a two-step telling.
note: Respond day for the end-of-unit assessment: at most four groups from the sheet's "not yet" cells, by form and by entry point; the others rehearse in pairs from the frame.

goal: Hook: the class weather chart from science; pose "What is it like, and what does it need?" and say today's weather.
note: Host: science grade K unit 2, weather watch (sk-weather-watch, school days 23 to 44), retrieved from the class's own chart.

goal: Hear a short weather report and point to the matching picture on the chart.
note: Retrieval task (first ten minutes): unit 1's text map, the topic and two facts, on a weather card.

goal: Take apart "It is ___" for weather (sunny, rainy, windy) and rebuild it; its job is to tell what the weather is like.
note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day.

goal: Say today's and yesterday's weather from the chart with weather picture cards.
SI Narrate as review: tell the week's weather in three parts (first, next, at the end) from the chart, one step harder than unit 2's two steps.
note: SI Narrate (WIDA.ELD-SI.K-3.Narrate, carried; owned in grade 3). Look-for: three parts in order with a time word.

goal: Tell the week's weather in three parts to a knee-to-knee partner, who says back one part.
Add one "because" to the weather chart ("We wear coats because it is cold"), framed for every entry point.
note: SI Explain begun (WIDA.ELD-SI.K-3.Explain, carried); unit 4 teaches explain in full.

goal: Build a short weather report with the teacher on a text map: today's weather as the topic, two facts beside it.
note: Model: text map, reviewed from unit 1, now on a science topic.

goal: Rehearse the weather report with the frames each entry point keeps; the "because" line is optional.
Keep the picture weather chart: draw and label today's weather and say the report to a partner.
Weather-report rounds: hear a partner's report, point to the chart picture, say it back.
Living things: hear a short description of what a plant needs and point to water and light on the picture.
note: Science grade K unit 4, living things and what they need (sk-living-needs), opens on school day 73 (week 15); before it the unit stayed on weather (frame "If later").

goal: Take apart "It needs ___" and "They have ___" and rebuild them; the job is to tell what a living thing must have.
note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day.

goal: Sort needs picture cards (water, food, light, air) into "a plant needs" and "an animal needs" and say each.
note: Home language: planta and plant, animal and animal are cognates.

goal: Build a short report on the class's plant with the teacher on a text map.
Draw and label a living thing and tell a partner what it needs, with the frame each entry point keeps.
note: First application day. Inform returns harder than unit 1: what a thing needs, not only how it looks (bar item 13). Withdrawal: entry points 5 and 6 work without the sentence frame from the next day.

goal: Build "It needs ___. It has ___." from cards about the class's plant and animal photos.
Tell the weather report to the class, then say a one-line report for the family note.
note: Change of audience. Candidate kept (bar item 10, one change of audience with the family): today, 0 days added. Family note in English and Spanish (spanish read).

goal: Self-check page: say what "needs" tells that "has" does not, and judge own report against the page.
note: Self-check page (kept by the student): name the form and its job in own words, then judge own language against the unit goal.

goal: Make alone: draw and label a short report on a living thing and tell it to a partner.
note: Withdrawal: last framed day for entry points 3 and 4 (frames off for the end-of-unit telling and drawing or writing task); entry points 1 and 2 keep the picture word bank and lose the cloze frame from the end-of-unit assessment.

goal: Hear a report and point to the picture, then give a report, with the picture word bank only.
note: Oral rehearsal of the unit forms with the picture word bank only; no new form.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: hear a report on a plant or animal not studied and match it to its picture; draw and label it; the teacher hears the first half of the talk tasks (tell what it needs).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 1 of 2 (about 30 minutes): the heard part and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the teacher hears about 15 talk tasks, about a minute each, while the others work. Look-fors per entry point on the paper sheet, "seen" or "not yet"; each item asks about each part of each code listed. Candidate kept (PRIME Breadth.LE, the year's second inform unit on a new standard): this assessment is its evidence; 0 days added. The new report is Curio Class's own.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: the second half of the talk tasks (tell the teacher what the new plant or animal needs).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 2 of 2: the other 15 talk tasks; students not being heard finish and check their page against the self-check. Each student is heard once.

goal: Respond: reteach "It needs" and the needs words in groups from the sheet.
note: Respond day for the end-of-unit assessment: at most four groups from the sheet's "not yet" cells, by form and by entry point; the others rehearse in pairs from the frame. Unit 3's record is carried unscored into the mid-year check that follows (frame).

goal: Kindergarten mid-year check, day 1: hear a new information page about a classroom object and point to its topic and facts; hear a new short story and order three pictures; draw the story's three parts in order and label one; the first half of the talk tasks.
note: Course-level check (30 minutes): the heard parts (each read or played twice) and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the talk task is heard one student at a time, about a minute each, while the others work, about 15 a day over the two days. Where one adult also gives math kindergarten's one-to-one check (days 84 and 85), the heard parts and drawing go today and every talk task goes on day 2 and the first minutes of the respond day.

goal: Kindergarten mid-year check, day 2: the second half of the talk tasks (describe a new object, or retell the story, as the sheet assigns).
note: Course-level check (30 minutes): the heard parts (each read or played twice) and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the talk task is heard one student at a time, about a minute each, while the others work, about 15 a day over the two days. Each student is heard once. Look-fors per entry point, "seen" or "not yet"; no scores stored. The talk tasks sample different ids from unit 3's end-of-unit talk task, so no evidence is collected twice.

goal: Respond to the mid-year check: groups by form and entry point from the sheet; any move between entry points is decided here.
note: At most four groups; the others rehearse in pairs from the frame.

goal: Hook: act out washing hands step by step; pose "What did we do, and what happened?" and name the words how and why.
note: Candidate kept (California 3.3, the language-need or learning-need note): the unit plan's teacher page carries it from today; 0 days added. The actions carry the meaning, so no one translates.

goal: Say how to do a class job in two or three steps and why we do it ("We wash hands so ___"), acting the steps with a partner.
Act out and tell class jobs (cleaning up blocks, washing hands) in steps with a partner, the reason last.
Hear the recount of the class's push test in order ("First we ___. Then ___.") and retell it to a partner before any cause is given.
note: SI Narrate as review (carried). Retrieval task: science grade K unit 1, pushes and pulls (school days 3 to 21), from its photos; any gentle push of a ball repeats the host's own step under its controls.

goal: Hear and say the question the class tested ("What if we push harder?") and match questions to test photos.
Meet the cause chain (two linked boxes: what we did, what happened) and fill it with the teacher from the push photos.
note: Model: cause chain, K to 1 stage, introduced.

goal: Take apart a "When ___, ___ because ___" sentence and rebuild it; "because" links a reason.
note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day. Candidate kept (PRIME Depth.ELD, a form taught as a feature with a job): today, 0 days added.

goal: Say what happened with push, pull, fast, slow and harder picture cards ("When we push harder, it goes fast").
Tell what was seen and the cause on the two boxes for a second push photo pair, with a partner.
Compare two ways the class tried (one hand or two): hear which worked better and say why.
Compare rounds with photo pairs: "This way worked better because ___".
Sun: hear what the class saw on the slide in sun and in shade, and the problem "How can we keep the slide cool?".
note: Science grade K unit 5, sunlight warms (sk-sun-warms), opens on school day 100 (week 20); before today the unit worked on pushes and pulls only (frame "If later"). Nothing is heated or shone in eyes.

goal: Say "In the sun it is warm. In the shade it is cool." with picture cards.
Fill a cause chain on the sun with the teacher: shade from a tree or from a sheet, and what happened.
Explain one push or sun test with two linked boxes to a partner, then draw it.
note: First application day. Withdrawal: entry points 5 and 6 work without the sentence frame from the next day.

goal: Explain a class job to a partner, then to a new classmate or the class puppet, and say what you added.
note: Change of audience and noticing what changed.

goal: How-to rounds with class job cards: the steps, then the reason last.
Compare the two shade tries and say which worked better and why, with a partner, then draw both.
Self-check page: say what "because" joins and judge own explanations against the page.
note: Self-check page (kept by the student): name the form and its job in own words, then judge own language against the unit goal.

goal: Make alone: explain a push or sun test on two linked boxes, drawn and labeled, and say which way worked better.
note: Withdrawal: last framed day for entry points 3 and 4 (frames off for the end-of-unit telling and drawing or writing task); entry points 1 and 2 keep the picture word bank and lose the cloze frame from the end-of-unit assessment.

goal: Build "When ___, ___ because ___" from cards about the unit's tests and say them.
Hear a cause and point to it, then tell a test, with the picture word bank only.
note: Oral rehearsal of the unit forms with the picture word bank only; no new form.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: view a new photo pair (a toy cart pushed gently and hard; a bench in sun and shade) and point to the cause and the question it answers; draw and label the two boxes; the teacher hears the first half of the talk tasks.
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 1 of 2 (about 30 minutes): the heard part and the drawing or writing task go to the whole class; the teacher hears about 15 talk tasks, about a minute each, while the others work. goal: End-of-unit assessment: the second half of the talk tasks (explain the photo pair to the teacher and say which way worked better; say how and why to do a class job).
note: End-of-unit assessment, day 2 of 2: the other 15 talk tasks; students not being heard finish and check their page against the self-check. Each student is heard once.

goal: Respond: reteach "When ___, ___" and "because" in groups from the sheet.
note: Respond day for the end-of-unit assessment: at most four groups from the sheet's "not yet" cells, by form and by entry point; the others rehearse in pairs from the frame.

note: Retrieval task (first ten minutes): unit 1's text map, topic and two facts.

note: Language Dive routine adapted from EL Education K-5 Language Arts (2017, CC BY 4.0), credited on the day.

goal: Match helper cards to place cards and say the sentence.
note: Home language: doctor and doctor, policía and police are cognates.

goal: Describe one helper to a partner from the text map; the partner points to the picture.
note: Change of audience, part 1: a partner.

goal: Helper rounds: hear a partner's description, pick the card, say it back.
Choose between two pictures and give one reason with "I like ___" and "I think ___ because ___".
note: Retrieval task: ELA grade K unit 1 taught opinion with a reason (ek-opinion, days 1 to 34); its frame opens today.

goal: Choice rounds: pick one of two pictured class activities and say why; the partner says "I agree" or "I disagree".

goal: Describe a helper to a partner, then draw and label it.

goal: Describe the same helper for the class's helper wall and say what changed from the partner telling.
